They refused to treat my dog, who had an urgent case of gastroenteritis and – after I had to go to another veterinarian – it turned out he had an infection/gastroenteritis and a fever of almost 40 degrees Celsius. I booked an urgent appointment for 6 am (after spending the night awake by his side), and they confirmed the appointment for 2 days later! Without noticing the absurdity of the 2-day timeframe, I went to the clinic and they wouldn't see him because they had appointments all morning! A SHAME. Our animals are like children and mine will never be treated this way again. I have never felt so hurt. Besides, I had been a client of theirs for quite some time! I will never set foot there again.

Unprofessionalism. Wrong diagnosis. I took my cat to this vet because he was very weak and thin. He was diagnosed with anemia and a weakened kidney. He was given medication for the anemia. My cat did not react well to this medication (vitamins) and rejected it. We called the vet and they told us to stop the medication. Three months later we went to the vet again to see how he was doing. We were told that the anemia had improved and that he could go home. On that same day, it was important to check the cat's weight to compare it with the previous weight from three months ago. However, they didn't have the previous weight recorded, and the vet from the last visit was no longer there. Furthermore, blood samples were taken and had to be repeated for reasons unknown. Not to mention the suffering my cat endured during these blood draws (bladder). Therefore, I took my cat to another vet after these unfortunate events. This new vet told me that my cat had kidney failure and an increasingly damaged kidney. And that the anemia was caused by the kidney. We found out that the main problem was the kidney, and it was never detected by this veterinarian, Serpa Pinto, which dragged on the suffering of my elderly cat for months. Furthermore, he gave us tips on how to feed my cat, and to this day he is a different cat, super healthy and happy. The current veterinarian I trust also cleaned the cat's teeth and prescribed medication, which he will have to take for the rest of his life to have a good quality of life and feel well. In short, this establishment disappointed me greatly, made a wrong diagnosis for my cat, demonstrated very little professionalism and little pride in caring for my cat. On top of that, we are talking about kidney failure, which is the number one cause of death in cats and must be treated immediately, which did not happen due to the diagnosis made. Incredulous. I do not recommend them.

I was very disappointed with the service I received, considering the excellent reviews this place had. I went to the appointment with my dog ​​who was bleeding. The vet told me she had to do a bladder ultrasound to see what was wrong. I agreed. She left the office and returned a few minutes later and said that there was no ultrasound machine after all. Then she said she would have to collect urine for analysis, took the dog away, returned a few minutes later and said she couldn't collect urine and gave me a small cup to take home and collect the urine myself. Then she said the dog had a lot of blood in his penis so an X-ray was needed. She did the X-ray but didn't see anything. She gave the dog an injection of something to relieve his pain, which we don't even know if he had. She prescribed a probiotic and told me I had to collect the urine and come back the next day. Of course, I had to go somewhere else because I wasn't going to leave my dog ​​bleeding for 24 hours without knowing what was wrong with him. It's a case of "thanks for nothing." And it's true, I paid almost €79.

Veterinary clinic that does not comply with the code of ethics of the OMV (Order of Veterinary Doctors).
I went to the hospital with a stray cat that was in an imminent emergency situation and they refused to help the animal unless a name and tax identification number (for billing) were provided, claiming that they would not provide treatment if we did not take responsibility for the animal. Obviously, I was never going to refuse to help the cat, and so I did. In the end, I questioned whether there was any possibility of the clinic being considerate of the exorbitant price they quoted me, always assuming the payment for the animal's treatment, however appealing to the common sense of the veterinarians, since they themselves are the ones who raise awareness about the adoption and rescue of stray animals and have the greatest responsibility because the code of ethics in the profession obliges them not to omit help for an animal in distress.
In response to my appeal, they said that this was impossible because the clinic did not make that type of agreement or protocols and if I did not have the money to pay at that moment, they would call the police (Nurse Rita). I advise no one to go to this place or promote it, as non-compliance with the code of ethics is unacceptable and should never be allowed!
